method_paragraph: Place discovery mass on the coincidence of a magnetic horizontal-gradient ridge (training_features band 3, tmi_hg) and an isostatic-gravity horizontal-gradient ridge (band 18, iso_grav_anom_hg), inside a positive geodetic dilatation lobe (band 8, geod_dilaterate), preferentially where that coincidence lies in a Faulds favorable setting computed only from the visible catalogue: a horse-tail ahead of a fault tip, a step-over corridor between two similarly striking tips, or a high-angle intersection with a visible strand. A rank-only Th/K weight (uint8 derivative, not a concentration) mildly boosts cells downslope-agnostic hydrothermal-alteration highs. Down-weight contour-parallel lidar steps, the named shoreline mimic, unless the cell is in a step-over. Do not use any prior submission raster, the ambiguous band-6 tc layer, or hidden labels as inputs. Emit 37654 binary dots at 3 px spacing, zero on mapped pixels and outside the footprint, all finite and in [0,1].
hypothesis: Expert faults missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue are enriched in Faulds favorable settings (step-overs, tip horse-tails, high-angle intersections) that sit on coincident magnetic and gravity ridges inside positive geodetic dilatation, rather than on the mid-segment of an already mapped range-front fault.
mechanism: Great Basin geothermal permeability concentrates where normal-fault step-overs, terminations and intersections raise fracture density and dilation (Faulds and Hinz, 2015). Those linking strands are the ones regional Quaternary compilations omit. They still offset basement density and magnetic markers, so horizontal-gradient ridges of isostatic gravity and total magnetic intensity coincide there, and regional GPS dilatation is positive.
named_non_fault_process: Pluvial Lake Lahontan shoreline and terrace risers, which are contour-parallel steps of similar height, plus flight-line-parallel magnetic levelling seams and GPS-station geometry artifacts in the dilatation grid.
why_not_already_in_catalogue: USGS Quaternary and INGENIOUS linework preferentially digitizes high-relief range-front scarps. Linking strands in a step-over and horse-tails at tips often have weaker or shorter geomorphic expression and are the structures Faulds and Hinz found host most Great Basin systems, not the mapped mid-segment.
difference_from_this_repo: Not E1 fabric-offset lag, not H79-NHR kernel-credit regression, not G79-STEPCO multi-field step dipoles, not G79B scarp-dipole persistence, not H79-FF far-field lidar ranking. No prior-submission raster is an input. Band 6 tc is unused because its semantics conflict (IR-79-13).
stop_rules: If any feature-alone symmetric AUC exceeds 0.90 and the feature is not provably computed without the withheld labels, stop before trusting the score.
Check surface rank-correlation and 3 px overlap against the registry before submission-dot placement.

Operative duplicate (IR-79-67, recorded before scores): Spearman > 0.90 against any raster, or forward 3 px overlap > 0.70 against a raster whose own 3 px halo covers at most 0.70 of allowed cells. Continuous surfaces use shared budget-matched-v3 dots. Literal positive-support overlap is printed and is not called uniqueness.
If the operative surface gate fails, do not place submission dots, do not retune, do not overlap-cap.
Do not mark ok_to_submit unless operative uniqueness, canaries, and both-seed holdout each beat the recorded H79-NHR holdout best, and the separate selector re-derives the gates.
Stop after this one experiment or two hours from registered_utc. No second method in this lane.
not_a_score: This file contains no holdout DTI, no leaderboard projection, and no organizer receipt.
